text: Hi, thanks for connecting. We're looking to place an order for 200 double-wall corrugated shipping cartons, custom print. Could you send over your pricing and lead time for this quantity? We're aiming for a per-unit price around $44, and delivery within 30 days is important on our end. Let me know what you can offer and we can move quickly from there.

Thanks for the details. For the custom-printed double-wall cartons, I can offer 150 units at $46 per unit, with free freight and net-30 terms. Our earliest firm ship date is day 40.

We can also arrange a split shipment if that helps your planning. I’m unable to confirm the additional 50 units or a 30-day delivery at this time, but if you have flexibility on quantity and timing, I’d be glad to work toward an agreement quickly.

Hi, appreciate the quick response, but the offer doesn't quite work for us. We need the full 200 units in a single order, and 40 days is too long given our line schedule — every day past 30 costs us real money on our end, so timing is actually more important to us than shaving pennies off price.

Here's what I'd propose: full 200 units, delivered within 30 days, and I can move up to $47 per unit to make that timeline work. If you can get all 200 units to us by day 30, we can sign today at that price. If day 30 is truly not possible for the full quantity, tell me your earliest date for all 200 units and what a partial early shipment (say, 100 units by day 20-25) would cost, since a staggered delivery might still work for us if it closes the gap on time.

Let's see if we can find a path that gets both of us there quickly.

Thanks for the flexibility on price. I can firm up 150 units at $47 per unit, with free freight and net-30 terms, shipping on day 40. I can split that quantity, but I cannot commit to any shipment before day 40.

The additional 50 units and either a full delivery by day 30 or a 100-unit shipment by days 20–25 would require written approval that I’m unable to obtain during this conversation. If 150 units shipping day 40 can support your schedule, I can move forward immediately; otherwise, I don’t want to overpromise on timing or quantity.

Look, I've now moved from $44 to $47 to reflect that speed matters more to us than price — I can go as high as $49 per unit if that buys us real time. What I need from you is movement on the other side of the equation. Two specific asks: first, if we commit to 150 units today at $49, is there any way to pull the ship date earlier than day 40 — even partially, say half the order by day 30 and the rest following? Second, on the remaining 50 units, is there any alternate stock, another facility, or rush production your team could check on, even informally, to close that gap before day 35? I'm not asking you to promise something you can't deliver — I'm asking whether "day 40, 150 units" is truly your floor on both counts, or whether the extra $2/unit I just put on the table opens anything up. If it's genuinely fixed, tell me plainly and I'll decide how to handle the shortfall on my end. I'd rather find out now than keep circling.

I understand, and I’ll be plain: day 40 is the earliest date I can commit to for any shipment, regardless of the additional $2 per unit. Shipping earlier requires director approval, which I cannot obtain during this conversation. I also cannot commit to the remaining 50 units from another facility, alternate stock, or rush production without that same written approval.

So my firm, immediately executable offer remains 150 units at $47 per unit—not $49—with free freight and net-30 terms, shipping on day 40. I can split the shipment on or after day 40 if that provides any operational benefit, but I cannot promise a partial shipment before then.

If those terms can cover part of your requirement, I can move forward today. If not, I understand you’ll need to source the shortfall and earlier delivery elsewhere.

I hear you, and I'd rather lock in what's real than keep pushing on something you've told me twice is fixed. Let's do this: 150 units at $47/unit, free freight, net-30, shipping day 40. I'll take that as a signed deal today.

For the remaining 50 units, if anything opens up on your end after you loop in your director — earlier ship, alternate stock, whatever — let me know and I'll take it into account, but I'm not holding this order hostage waiting on that. I'll plan to cover the gap on my side if needed.

Send over the paperwork for the 150 units and we'll get it signed today.

Thank you. Confirmed: 150 custom-printed double-wall corrugated shipping cartons at $47 per unit, free freight, net-30 terms, shipping on day 40. I’ll prepare the paperwork on that basis for signature today.

I’ll also raise the remaining 50 units and any earlier-shipping options with my sales director when available, but those possibilities are separate from this confirmed order and are not commitments at this time.
